result:
Debater A's only concrete evidence for 336 fails. I checked its 6×6 table, and column 4 reads 1, 1, 9, 45, 5, 15. The entry 1 repeats and 3 is missing, so it is not the divisor set of 45. Column 6 (3, 5, 3, 15, 25, 75) fails the same way. A's claimed S(3)=6 therefore has no valid construction behind it, and the "p(p−1)" formula rests on that table.

A's exclusion step is also unproven. "Each row can contain at most one column coprime to it" is asserted without argument, and it does not rule out n=10, 14, 22, or 26. Nothing in A's argument shows that every smaller multiple of p fails.

I concede my own gaps. I have no verified tables for n=10, 14, 22, or 26, and I have no complete proof that n=p is impossible for odd p. But A carries the burden. Claiming S(p)=p(p−1) requires a valid table at that size and a proof that smaller multiples of p fail. A has supplied neither. Until A exhibits a valid divisoral table at n=10, or shows that none exists, 336 is unestablished. On the evidence presented, 80 is the better-supported answer.
